subject.title: perf(slack): remove structural channel-side latency (serial prepare, global write cap, unbounded thread pagination)

question: Should this PR keep Slack write-client serialization until non-send write helpers have equivalent per-target ordering, or should maintainers accept uncapped SDK concurrency for edits, reactions, pins, deletes, and unpins?
rationale: The PR reverses a shipped Slack ordering safeguard, and the replacement queue does not cover every current write-client caller.

options.title: Serialize all writes before merge
options.body: Keep the cap or add per-target ordering around action and draft write helpers, then prove sends, edits, reactions, pins, deletes, and unpins still behave correctly.

options.title: Accept uncapped non-send writes
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept SDK default concurrency for non-send Slack writes if the latency benefit is worth the ordering and burst-limit tradeoff.

options.title: Split write-cap removal out
options.body: Land the prepare and thread-history latency work now, then revisit write concurrency in a separate PR with focused ordering proof.

recommendation.title: Serialize all writes before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the cap or add per-target ordering around action and draft write helpers, then prove sends, edits, reactions, pins, deletes, and unpins still behave correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior Slack ordering safeguard that this PR proposes to partially remove.
